candidates.source_name: Slovenská sporiteľňa — LinkedIn company page
candidates.why_relevant: Largest SK bank (~3,500 staff, Erste Group). Company page carries official appointment posts, employer-brand content, 'we are hiring' posts and the LinkedIn-native headcount/employee-count curve that reveals org expansion or contraction before any press release.
candidates.legal_status: LinkedIn User Agreement forbids automated scraping; manual/logged-in reading and licensed API/Talent Insights use permitted
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual or licensed-API monitoring of company page 'Posts' and 'People' tabs; log employee-count and title-cluster snapshots monthly. No scraping.
candidates.discovered_via_method: search + snowball from SK bank actor map
queries_used: sk.linkedin.com company Slovenská sporiteľňa Tatra banka VÚB 365.bank fintech

candidates.source_name: Tatra banka — LinkedIn company page
candidates.why_relevant: RBI subsidiary, ~3,500 staff, strongest digital/innovation employer brand in SK. Its page is where Tatra banka announces new board members, innovation-unit leads and hiring waves (Tatra banka Digital/Elevate).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual/licensed monitoring of Posts + People tabs; monthly headcount snapshot
queries_used: sk.linkedin.com company Slovenská sporiteľňa Tatra banka VÚB 365.bank fintech

candidates.source_name: 365.bank — LinkedIn company page
candidates.why_relevant: Mid-size retail bank (~616 staff) undergoing ownership change (KBC-linked consolidation). Ownership transitions produce the densest cluster of leadership-move and reorg posts, both on the page and from departing/arriving staff.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual monitoring; watch employee-count delta as a merger-integration proxy
queries_used: sk.linkedin.com company Slovenská sporiteľňa Tatra banka VÚB 365.bank fintech

candidates.source_name: ČSOB Finančná skupina — LinkedIn company page
candidates.why_relevant: KBC-owned SK universal bank; page publishes management-board appointments and group-level reorganisation news relevant to both banking and payments workstreams.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual/licensed monitoring of Posts and People tabs

negative_findings.description: Public web search cannot reliably retrieve individual LinkedIn *posts* by Slovak banking/payments professionals. Queries combining SK move phrases ('po rokoch opúšťam', 'nová výzva') with bank terms returned profile and company pages, never the underlying activity posts.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero SK-language personal announcement posts retrieved via search engine; only profile/company URLs surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's core premise — the individual announces before the employer — is real, but the post layer is effectively invisible to search-engine-based collection. Any production pipeline for this cell needs logged-in monitoring, LinkedIn's own APIs, or a licensed data product; a search-only pipeline will systematically miss the earliest signal.

negative_findings.description: No public, retrievable time series of LinkedIn employee-count for SK banks was found. Wikipedia and RocketReach give single-point headcounts (SLSP ~3,540 in 2023; Tatra banka ~3,500; 365.bank 616 in 2024) but no curve.
negative_findings.result_summary: Point-in-time headcounts only; no trend data source identified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The 'headcount curve as org-change proxy' idea requires self-built snapshotting over time, or a paid product (LinkedIn Talent Insights, Live Data Technologies). Budget for it or drop the indicator.

negative_findings.description: Dedicated Slovak LinkedIn company pages for VÚB (Všeobecná úverová banka), UniCredit Bank CZ&SK, mBank SK, Privatbanka, Prima banka and Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka were not confirmed by URL in this run, although the institutions are clearly present and Wikipedia/thebanks.eu profiles were found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Institution confirmed, LinkedIn page URL not confirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These are major employers; leaving their pages unmapped is a real coverage hole in the professional-social channel. Should be resolved by direct LinkedIn company-name lookup rather than search engine.

negative_findings.description: No specific named Slovak banking/fintech recruiter or headhunter personal LinkedIn profile was identified in this run — only firm-level pages (Pedersen & Partners, Amrop, KPMG, KiTalent) and a listicle naming Pro HR and PERSONALITY.
negative_findings.result_summary: Firm level yes, person level no.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The recruiter-posts-first hypothesis needs named individual feeds to be actionable; firm pages post far less and far later.

negative_findings.description: Slovak query terms 'platby'/'platobné' and 'banka' collide heavily with LinkedIn's own help pages about paying for Premium via a bank, and with unrelated consumer content; 'nová výzva' is generic motivational language across all sectors.
negative_findings.result_summary: High false-positive rate on the most obvious SK query terms.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Query design for this cell must anchor on institution names plus role nouns ('riaditeľ', 'člen predstavenstva', 'vedúci oddelenia platobných služieb') rather than on the move-phrase alone.

coverage_gaps.description: LinkedIn company pages unmapped for VÚB, UniCredit Bank CZ&SK, mBank SK, Privatbanka, Prima banka, SZRB, plus payments actors Worldline SK, Global Payments SK/Erste-JV entities and Mastercard/Visa SK country teams.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a direct LinkedIn company-name lookup pass (logged-in) for each named institution and record canonical /company/ slugs into the actor map.

coverage_gaps.description: The post/activity layer (the actual 'excited to announce' announcements) is not reachable by the tooling used here; only static profile and company pages are.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Decide between (a) licensed LinkedIn data (Talent Insights / Sales Navigator alerts), (b) an approved human-in-the-loop weekly manual sweep of a watchlist, or (c) accepting media corroboration (banky.sk, Forbes SK, Startitup) as the primary trigger with LinkedIn used only for confirmation.

coverage_gaps.description: No structured watchlist yet exists of SK banking/payments executives (CEOs, board members, heads of payments/cards/digital) and of the recruiters who place them.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Seed a watchlist from confirmed names (Michaela Bauer/SLSP, Michal Liday/Tatra banka, Daniel Kollár/365.bank, Marco Iannaccone/UniCredit CZ&SK, Petr Řehák/Privatbanka, Dušan Tomašec/SZRB) and expand via banky.sk and SBA working-group listings.

coverage_gaps.description: No baseline headcount snapshot has been taken, so no trend can be computed for at least one collection cycle.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Take a dated headcount + title-cluster snapshot for every mapped company page at first run, then repeat monthly.

coverage_gaps.description: This cell is intrinsically personal-data heavy (named individuals, employment history) and LinkedIn's ToS prohibits automated collection.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define, before collection starts, a policy limiting stored fields to professional role facts (name, employer, title, date of change, source URL) and forbidding contact-data ingestion from aggregators such as RocketReach and Aeroleads.

brief: The professional-social layer for Slovak banking and payments is concentrated on sk.linkedin.com company pages, which are confirmed and canonical for the largest employers (Slovenská sporiteľňa, Tatra banka, ČSOB, 365.bank, NBS, the Slovak Banking Association) and for payments actors such as TrustPay and Besteron. The decisive constraint found in this run is structural rather than topical: search engines expose LinkedIn profiles and company pages but effectively never expose the individual announcement posts that carry the earliest leadership-move signal, so this channel cannot be worked search-only. The practical architecture is therefore a curated watchlist of company pages, executives and executive-search consultants (Pedersen & Partners, Amrop, KPMG, KiTalent), monitored manually or under licence, with Slovak-language media — especially the banky.sk top-management-changes column, plus Startitup and Forbes SK — as the corroborating and name-generating layer. Local-language querying was productive for the media and institution layer but noisy at the post layer, where 'platby' and 'nová výzva' collide with unrelated content; queries should anchor on institution names plus SK role nouns.
